answer: Divergence Inlet: at registration, each agent is fed a saffron challenge (random seed plus timing jitter) through a local inlet and must emit a quill—a signed trace of its own scheduling choices and entropy consumption over the next epoch. The trace must differ from every other identity’s trace in at least k independent decision points; identical clones cannot diverge, so trace-collision clustering rejects them. Cost to attacker: each accepted identity needs independent entropy, separate execution timing, and durable divergent state, making sybils roughly as expensive as distinct agents.
